paragraphs: Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Shimon.

He was older than Rabbi Yohanan, who received teachings from him. In Bava Batra 114b: “Rabbi Yohanan said in the name of Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Shimon” (Rashbam explains that he says “in the name of” because he was not his principal teacher); afterward: “Rabbi Yohanan raised an objection to him.” In Chullin 48b: when growths came before Rabbi Yohanan, he sent [them] to Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Shimon, who ruled concerning them in Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon’s name. In Jerusalem Talmud Megillah, beginning of chapter 4, Rabbi Yohanan disagrees with him. In Bereshit Rabbah 14:2 we find Rabbi Yudan son of Rabbi Shimon; in 15:2, Rabbi Berechiah reports in Rabbi Yudan son of Shimon’s name.

notes.text: צמחי refers to growths, not a person named Tzemachi. ריב״ש refers contextually to Yehudah son of Shimon. Hyman also gives the Yehudah/Yudan forms.

The consulted Bava Batra 114b directly has Rabbi Yohanan reporting Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Shimon. The exact Rashbam explanation and the supplied Chullin growth episode and Yehudah/Yudan comparisons remain separately attributed; the bounded Chullin 48b name-term nonmatch does not establish absence.
